    Village SnacksMeeko's biscuitsHot buttermilk biscuits. Better than a ship's biscuit.How to make it100g cold butter, diced450g self-raising flour1/2 tsp salt300ml buttermilk50g butter, for spreading3 tbsp honeyRub the cold butter into the flour and salt.Stir in the buttermilk until it just comes together.Pat out and cut into rounds.Bake at 220°C until tall and golden.Split while warm and spread with butter and honey.Grandmother Willow's harvest nutsMaple pecans and walnuts. The spinning arrow points to John SmithHow to make it100g pecans100g walnuts50g pepitas4 tbsp maple syrup1/2 tsp sea salt flakesToss the pecans, walnuts and pepitas with the maple syrup and salt.Spread on a lined tray.Roast at 170°C for a few minutes, stirring once.Cool completely so they set.Break into rough clusters.River corn fritters with lime cremaSweet kernels, spring onion and chilli fried crisp and lacy, zingy sour cream dip, smoked saltHow to make itNot on tonight's cookSweet corn fritters with spring onion and chilli, fried crisp and lacy, with a zingy lime and sour cream dip and a pinch of smoked salt.Mix 400g corn kernels with 100g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 2 eggs, 80ml milk, 3 sliced spring onions, 1 chopped red chilli and salt.Heat oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry heaped tablespoons for 2 minutes a side until golden and crisp.Drain on paper towel.Mix 200g sour cream with the zest and juice of 1 lime.Sprinkle the fritters with smoked salt and serve with the crema.Smoked river trout with wild greensJust around the riverbend, caught this morning.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.From the CookfireVirginia harvest stewChicken thighs, pumpkin, corn, kidney beans and tomato with smoked paprikaHow to make it600g chicken thighs, diced1 tbsp olive oil500g butternut pumpkin, diced1 can corn kernels1 can kidney beans, drained1 can crushed tomatoes1 tsp smoked paprika150g fine cornmeal150g plain flour2 tsp baking powder1 egg250ml milk2 tbsp vegetable oilDice the chicken and pumpkin.Brown the chicken in the oil.Add the pumpkin, corn, beans, tomatoes and paprika.Simmer until thick and the pumpkin is tender.Meanwhile mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder, egg, milk and oil into a batter.Pour into a greased tin and bake at 200°C until golden.Serve the stew with slices of cornbread.Jamestown beef and onion pieBeef and onion pie for the settlers digging for Ratcliffe's gold.How to make itNot on tonight's cookBeef chuck slow cooked with sweet onions, thyme and stock until rich, baked under a golden puff pastry lid with mustard on the side.Toss 1kg diced beef chuck in 2 tbsp plain flour and brown in batches.Soften 3 sliced onions, then add the beef, 600ml beef stock, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce and thyme.Cover and simmer 2 hours until tender and thick, then cool slightly.Spoon into a pie dish, cover with a puff pastry sheet, brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes.Serve with hot English mustard.Sweet ThingsMaple roasted peachesPeach halves roasted with butter and maple syrupHow to make it4 ripe peaches50g butter4 tbsp maple syrup500ml vanilla ice cream50g pecans, crushedHalve the peaches and remove the stones.Sit cut side up in a baking dish, dot with butter and drizzle with maple syrup.Roast at 200°C until soft and syrupy.Crush the pecans.Serve warm with ice cream and pecans on top.Gourds and CupsFlit's blueberry mint coolerBlueberries and mint. Flit prefers Kocoum to John SmithHow to make it150g blueberries1/2 cup mint leaves2 limes2 tbsp honey500ml cranberry juice500ml sparkling water3 cups crushed iceMuddle most of the blueberries with the mint, lime juice and honey in a jug until the berries burst.Stir in the cranberry juice and chill.Fill glasses with crushed ice and pour in the berry mix to halfway.Top with sparkling water and garnish with blueberries and a mint sprig.Sassafras root teaMeeko's paws stay off this one.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
